context.analysis:
## Overview
[The Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for EU and US patients. It ensures strict regional data residency, regulatory compliance, and interoperability across dual GCP environments.]

## Key Elements
- Patients (EU/US) and Licensed Clinicians
- GeoDNS (Anycast)
- API Gateway / Edge Proxy
- Web/Mobile Client App
- Core Telehealth Service
- AI Symptom Checker Service
- Consent & Policy Engine
- Interoperability / Integration Service
- Audit & Compliance Logger Container
- Video Streaming / SFU (LiveKit/Mediasoup)
- GCP Cloud SQL (PostgreSQL) and GCP Cloud Storage
- GCP Pub/Sub
- External Systems: National Pharmacies, National EHR Gateways, Payment Gateways (Stripe), Notification Providers (Twilio/Firebase)

## Relationships
- Patients/Clinicians to API Gateway via HTTPS, WebSockets, and WebRTC (UDP/TCP)
- Client to Video SFU via WebRTC
- Interoperability Service to US Pharmacies/EHRs via HL7 FHIR over REST/TLS
- Interoperability Service to EU Pharmacies/EHRs via National e-Prescription APIs over REST/TLS
- Containers to Pub/Sub via gRPC
- Containers to Regional Databases and Cloud Storage via HTTPS/REST (TLS 1.3)
- Platform to Payment and Notification Providers via HTTPS/REST

## Technology Stack
- Cloud Provider: GCP (`europe-west3` for EU, `us-central1` for US) to enforce regional data isolation
- Routing: GeoDNS for regional entry points
- Real-Time Media: WebRTC and SFU (LiveKit/Mediasoup) for low-bandwidth degradation (<300 kbit/s)
- Messaging: GCP Pub/Sub for asynchronous event-driven architecture
- Storage: GCP Cloud SQL (PostgreSQL) and GCP Cloud Storage with Customer-Managed Encryption Keys (CMEK)
- Interoperability: HL7 FHIR (US) and National e-Prescription APIs (EU)

## Rationale
- Dual-region GCP deployments with strict network separation guarantee GDPR and HIPAA compliance while keeping health data within its required jurisdiction.
- Decoupled microservices, regional databases, and specialized SFU media streaming ensure high availability, traceability for EU MDR, and robust performance for rural users.

containers.analysis:
## Overview
A cross-border telehealth platform providing video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for EU and US patients. It enforces strict regional data residency and compliance using isolated cloud infrastructure.

## Key Elements
- Patients (EU/US) and Licensed Clinicians
- API Gateway & Consent Container (Envoy / Google Cloud Endpoints, Open Policy Agent)
- Core Telehealth Backend (Node.js/Go)
- Video Consultation Service (WebRTC / Janus Media Server on GCE MIGs)
- AI Symptom Checker (Python / FastAPI)
- Interoperability Adapter (Java / Spring Boot)
- Asynchronous Event Broker (GCP Pub/Sub)
- Dedicated Audit & Logging Container (Fluentbit / OpenTelemetry)
- Regional Databases (Cloud SQL PostgreSQL, Cloud Storage, Cloud Firestore)
- External Systems: National Pharmacies, National EHR Gateways, Payment Gateways (Stripe), Notification Providers (Twilio/Firebase)

## Relationships
- Patients/Clinicians to API Gateway via HTTPS/WSS
- Video Clients to Janus Media Server via WebRTC (UDP/TCP)
- API Gateway to Consent Container and Core Backend via gRPC over mTLS
- Core Backend to GCP Pub/Sub for asynchronous event distribution
- Interoperability Adapter to National Gateways and Pharmacies via mTLS over HTTPS
- Backends and AI containers to Audit Container via gRPC

## Technology Stack
- Google Cloud Platform (GCP): Multi-region deployment in `europe-west3` and `us-central1` for data residency.
- GCP VPC Service Perimeter (VPC-SC): Network-level isolation between regions.
- Google Cloud Run & GKE Autopilot: Stateless container orchestration for APIs, AI, and adapters.
- Google Compute Engine (GCE) Managed Instance Groups: Stateful media streaming for WebRTC.
- GCP Pub/Sub: Asynchronous event messaging and system decoupling.
- Cloud SQL PostgreSQL & Cloud Storage: Region-locked transactional storage with WORM immutability.

## Rationale
Isolated regional container clusters and VPC-SC enforce strict GDPR and HIPAA data residency constraints. Decoupled microservices, scalable WebRTC media servers, and asynchronous messaging ensure low-bandwidth resilience and high availability for rural users.

API Gateway & Consent Container.analysis:
## Overview
- Cross-Border Telehealth Platform providing video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for EU and US patients.
- Designed with strict regional data residency, consent management, and low-latency handling for unstable connections on GCP.

## Key Elements
- Patients (EU/US) and Licensed Clinicians
- API Gateway & Consent Container (Envoy Proxy, Open Policy Agent, WASM claims extension)
- Core Telehealth Backend (Node.js / Go, Appointment & Consultation Service, E-Prescription Domain Module)
- Video Consultation Service (WebRTC / Janus Media Server on GCP MIGs)
- AI Symptom Checker (Python / FastAPI)
- Interoperability Adapter (Java / Spring Boot)
- Dedicated Audit & Logging Container (Fluentbit / OpenTelemetry)
- Regional Databases (Cloud SQL PostgreSQL, Cloud Storage, Cloud Firestore in `europe-west3` and `us-central1`)

## Relationships
- Patients & Clinicians -> API Gateway & Consent Container via HTTPS/WSS
- API Gateway & Consent Container -> Core Telehealth Backend via gRPC over mTLS
- API Gateway & Consent Container -> AI Symptom Checker via gRPC over mTLS
- Policy Enforcement Engine -> Dedicated Audit & Logging Container via OpenTelemetry / gRPC
- Core Telehealth Backend -> Regional Databases via SQL over mTLS

## Technology Stack
- GCP (`europe-west3`, `us-central1`): Enforces regional data residency constraints.
- Envoy Proxy: Manages ingress TLS, WSS signaling, and gRPC routing.
- Open Policy Agent (OPA): Evaluates consent scopes and regional policies.
- WebRTC / Janus Media Server: Delivers video consultations with degraded bandwidth fallback.
- HL7 FHIR & National Standards: Ensures interoperability for US and EU pharmacies.

## Rationale
- Decouples perimeter security and consent enforcement via OPA and Envoy to guarantee GDPR and HIPAA compliance.
- Uses regional GCP deployments and gRPC communication to minimize latency for rural, unstable connections.

Core Telehealth Backend.analysis:
## Overview
The Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides secure video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for patients in the EU and US. The system ensures strict data residency, privacy compliance (GDPR/HIPAA), and AI output traceability.

## Key Elements
- Patients (EU/US) and Licensed Clinicians
- Core Telehealth Backend (Go-based micro-components: Consultation Orchestrator, E-Prescription Workflow, Consent Enforcement Middleware, Symptom Checker Orchestrator, Patient Profile & Consent Manager, Event Dispatcher, Outbox Pattern Handler)
- Video Consultation Service (WebRTC / Janus Media Server on GCE MIGs)
- AI Symptom Checker (Python / FastAPI)
- Interoperability Adapter (Java / Spring Boot)
- Asynchronous Event Broker (GCP Pub/Sub with region-pinned topics)
- Dedicated Audit & Logging Container (Fluentbit / OpenTelemetry)
- Regional Databases (Cloud SQL PostgreSQL, Cloud Storage, Cloud Firestore)
- External Systems: National Pharmacies, National EHR Gateways, Stripe, Twilio/Firebase

## Relationships
- Consultation Orchestrator -> Video Consultation Service: Manages media streams [gRPC]
- E-Prescription Workflow -> Interoperability Adapter: Dispatches national-format payloads [gRPC]
- Symptom Checker Orchestrator -> AI Symptom Checker: Requests urgency recommendations [gRPC]
- Event Dispatcher -> Asynchronous Event Broker: Publishes sanitized domain events to region-pinned topics [gRPC/Protobuf]
- All Components -> Regional Databases: Enforces geo-pinned data storage [PostgreSQL wire protocol]
- Core Telehealth Backend -> Dedicated Audit & Logging Container: Sends audit logs [gRPC]

## Technology Stack
- Core Telehealth Backend: Go for high throughput and low latency micro-components
- Cloud Platform: Google Cloud Platform (GCP regions europe-west3 and us-central1)
- Messaging: GCP Pub/Sub with region-pinned topics and Outbox Pattern for eventual consistency
- Video Streaming: WebRTC and Janus Media Server on GCE MIGs
- Interoperability & Compliance: HL7 FHIR (US), national e-prescription standards (EU), Open Policy Agent for consent

## Rationale
This architecture enforces strict regional data residency by isolating EU and US data through region-pinned databases and message topics, ensuring full GDPR and HIPAA compliance. Furthermore, the Go-based micro-component design with transactional outbox patterns guarantees resilience under unstable network conditions while maintaining EU MDR traceability via immutable audit logs.

## Overview
- Cross-Border Telehealth Platform providing video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for EU and US patients.
- Designed to ensure regional data residency, strict regulatory compliance (GDPR/HIPAA), and robust performance for unstable rural internet connections.

## Key Elements
- Patients (EU/US) and Licensed Clinicians
- API Gateway & Consent Container (Envoy / Google Cloud Endpoints, Open Policy Agent)
- Core Telehealth Backend (Node.js / Go)
- Video Consultation Service Container:
  - Signaling Controller (Node.js / WebSockets)
  - Media Router / SFU Core (Janus Media Server / C++)
  - Adaptive Bitrate & Quality Manager (C++ plugin)
  - Room Access Control & Consent Verifier (Node.js)
  - Recording & Transcoding Worker (Python / GStreamer)
  - TURN/STUN Relay Manager (Coturn on GCE Compute Engine)
- AI Symptom Checker (Python / FastAPI)
- Interoperability Adapter (Java / Spring Boot)
- Asynchronous Event Broker (GCP Pub/Sub)
- Dedicated Audit & Logging Container (Fluentbit / OpenTelemetry)
- Regional Databases (Cloud SQL PostgreSQL, Cloud Storage, Cloud Firestore in `europe-west3` and `us-central1`)
- External Systems: National Pharmacies, National EHR Gateways, Stripe, Twilio/Firebase

## Relationships
- Patients and Clinicians connect to Media Router and TURN/STUN Relay Manager via WebRTC (DTLS-SRTP over UDP/TCP) and TURN.
- Signaling Controller communicates with API Gateway via gRPC for session authorization.
- Signaling Controller queries Room Access Control & Consent Verifier via internal gRPC to validate real-time consent and data residency.
- Recording & Transcoding Worker streams encrypted media chunks to Regional Cloud Storage via HTTPS (REST).
- Media Router emits session telemetry to Audit & Logging Container via OpenTelemetry (gRPC).

## Technology Stack
- Google Cloud Platform (GCP) across `europe-west3` and `us-central1` for strict data residency.
- Janus Media Server and Coturn for real-time video streaming and NAT traversal.
- Node.js, Python, Java, and Go for backend microservices and components.
- PostgreSQL, Cloud Firestore, and Cloud Storage for regional persistent data storage.
- WebRTC, gRPC, WebSockets, and HTTPS (REST/TLS) for communication protocols.

## Rationale
- The multi-region GCP architecture guarantees that EU health data remains in `europe-west3` and US data in `us-central1` to satisfy GDPR and HIPAA.
- Janus SFU combined with a custom Adaptive Bitrate Manager and Coturn relay ensures seamless video consultations even on unstable rural connections below 300 kbit/s.

AI Symptom Checker.analysis:
## Overview
The Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for patients in the EU and US. It enforces strict regional data residency, GDPR/HIPAA compliance, and EU MDR traceability constraints on GCP.

## Key Elements
- Patients (EU/US) and Licensed Clinicians
- API Gateway & Consent Container (Envoy / Google Cloud Endpoints, Open Policy Agent)
- Core Telehealth Backend (Node.js / Go)

  - Local Audit & State Store (SQLite / Cloud SQL proxy)
  - Async Event Publisher (`asyncio`)
- Interoperability Adapter (Java / Spring Boot)
- Asynchronous Event Broker (GCP Pub/Sub)
- Dedicated Audit & Logging Container (Fluentbit / OpenTelemetry)
- Regional Databases (Cloud SQL PostgreSQL, Cloud Storage, Cloud Firestore in `europe-west3` and `us-central1`)

- API Gateway -> AI Symptom Checker: Routes symptom check requests [gRPC over mTLS]
- API Router -> Inference Orchestrator: Manages symptom analysis [In-process]
- Inference Orchestrator -> Model Version Tracker: Logs metadata [In-process]

- Clinical Safety Guardrail Filter -> Dedicated Audit & Logging Container: Sends raw vs. filtered logs [gRPC]
- AI Symptom Checker -> Regional Databases: Persists check histories [gRPC/SQL]

## Technology Stack
- Cloud Provider: GCP (`europe-west3` for EU, `us-central1` for US) ensuring strict regional data residency.
- AI Symptom Checker: Python with FastAPI for high-performance async processing.
- AI/ML Services: Vertex AI for regional LLM deployments.
- Guardrails: LangChain Guardrails for clinical safety validation.
- Messaging: GCP Pub/Sub for asynchronous event streaming.
- Protocols: gRPC, mTLS, HTTPS, and SQL for secure inter-component and cross-container communication.

## Rationale
This architecture segregates data regionally to comply with GDPR and HIPAA mandates while enforcing EU MDR traceability via dedicated model version tracking and audit logs. Asynchronous event publishing and regional LLM routing ensure high availability, low latency, and adherence to strict clinical safety standards.

Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides secure video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for EU and US patients. The architecture uses GCP regions to strictly enforce regional data residency and compliance.

## Key Elements
- Patients (EU/US) and Licensed Clinicians
- External Systems: National Pharmacies, National EHR Gateways, Payment Gateways (Stripe), Notification Providers (Twilio/Firebase)

- Node.js, Go, Python, Java: Microservices runtime environments per container specification

## Rationale
The architecture strictly confines EU health data to `europe-west3` and US data to `us-central1` to satisfy GDPR and HIPAA mandates. Attribute-based event routing and schema validation ensure resilience for low-bandwidth connections and complete audit traceability for AI medical outputs.

Dedicated Audit & Logging Container.analysis:
## Overview
Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for patients across the EU and US. It ensures strict data residency, regulatory compliance (GDPR, HIPAA, EU MDR), and auditability through regionally isolated infrastructure.

## Key Elements
- Patients (EU/US) and Licensed Clinicians
- Dedicated Audit & Logging Container (deployed in `europe-west3` and `us-central1`)
- Log Collector (Fluent Bit)
- Audit & Compliance Engine (OpenTelemetry Collector)
- Compliance Archival Manager (Go-based cron)
- Log Access Proxy
- Regional Cloud Storage (Immutable Buckets with Object Lock)

## Relationships
- Core Telehealth Backend / AI Symptom Checker -> Log Collector [gRPC]
- Log Collector -> Audit & Compliance Engine [In-memory / IPC]
- Audit & Compliance Engine -> Compliance Archival Manager [Internal gRPC]
- Compliance Archival Manager -> Regional Cloud Storage [HTTPS / Storage API with CMEK and Object Lock]
- External Compliance Auditors -> Log Access Proxy [HTTPS / mTLS]
- Log Access Proxy -> Regional Cloud Storage [HTTPS / IAM]

## Technology Stack
- Google Cloud Platform (GCP): Target cloud provider for managed infrastructure and regional isolation (`europe-west3`, `us-central1`).
- Fluent Bit: Lightweight log ingestion and PHI stripping at the edge.
- OpenTelemetry Collector: Normalization and structured schema tagging for AI traceability (R-07).
- Go: Language for the Compliance Archival Manager component.

## Rationale
The architecture enforces strict geographic isolation by deploying independent logging pipelines per region to satisfy EU and US data residency mandates. Immutable WORM storage and OpenTelemetry tracing ensure rigorous compliance with HIPAA, GDPR, and EU MDR auditability requirements.

Regional Databases.analysis:
## Overview
The Cross-Border Telehealth Platform provides secure video consultations, e-prescriptions, and an AI symptom checker for EU and US patients on GCP. It enforces strict regional data residency and GDPR/HIPAA compliance via isolated components in `europe-west3` and `us-central1`.

## Key Elements
- Transactional Store (Cloud SQL PostgreSQL)
- Document & Audit Store (Cloud Firestore)
- Blob Storage (Cloud Storage)
- Data Encryption Manager (Cloud KMS)
- Database Migration & Schema Manager (Flyway / Cloud Build)
- Regional Replica Router (Cloud SQL Proxy / Built-in HA)
- Database Backup & Retention Manager (Cloud Backup and DR / Storage Lifecycle)

## Relationships
- Core Telehealth Backend -> Transactional Store: Read/Write patient data and consent policies [TCP / PostgreSQL Wire Protocol]
- AI Symptom Checker -> Document & Audit Store: Write cryptographically signed audit logs [gRPC]
- Transactional Store, Document & Audit Store, Blob Storage -> Data Encryption Manager: Encrypt/Decrypt regional data at rest [Cloud KMS API / gRPC]
- Interoperability Adapter -> Transactional Store: Read/Write FHIR/national e-prescription data [TCP / PostgreSQL Wire Protocol]
- Database Migration & Schema Manager -> Transactional Store: Apply localized schema migrations [TCP / PostgreSQL Wire Protocol]
- Core Telehealth Backend -> Regional Replica Router: Route read-heavy queries to regional replicas [TCP / PostgreSQL Wire Protocol]
- Regional Replica Router -> Transactional Store: Replicate transactional data within the same region [TCP]
- Database Backup & Retention Manager -> Transactional Store & Blob Storage: Execute regional snapshots and lifecycle archival [GCP Internal API]

## Technology Stack
- Cloud SQL PostgreSQL: Region-locked relational storage for patient records and e-prescriptions
- Cloud Firestore: Document storage capturing immutable AI symptom-checker inputs and model versions
- Cloud Storage: Encrypted object storage for consultation artifacts with CMEK
- Cloud KMS: Regional Customer-Managed Encryption Keys ensuring cryptographic isolation
- Cloud SQL Proxy / Built-in HA: Localized read-scaling and automatic failover

## Rationale
This architecture uses region-locked GCP services and KMS encryption to strictly satisfy EU/US data residency mandates. Component separation ensures traceability, compliance, and disaster recovery.
